columns.label: Ebook
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily get and consume ebooks on the platform (free or paid) as a first-class product, open, buy, borrow, or read without hunting.

columns.label: Short-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily consume short-form video as a first-class surface (For You, Reels, Shorts).

columns.label: Long-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch creator / UGC long-form video (or specialty long video) as a core surface. Course lectures belong under Courses. Hollywood catalogs belong under Series/Films.

columns.label: Series/Films
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch series and films as an SVOD / catalog entertainment product.

columns.label: Courses
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily take or browse structured courses as a first-class product.

columns.label: Newsletters
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily read or subscribe to newsletters / creator writing as a first-class product.

columns.label: Audio
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily listen to music, podcasts, or audiobooks as a first-class product.

columns.label: Memberships
columns.definition: Yes if a creator or seller can accept payments from others and make money through the platform, checkout, fan subscriptions, tips, ads, shop, or creator funds. Not only a classic Patreon-style membership product.

columns.label: Community & Messaging
columns.definition: Yes if you can create or join a group, community, or club, including group chats, Groups, subreddits, community tabs, discussion boards, or community feeds. A one-off comment on a single video or listing is not the bar; a durable place for the group to talk is.

columns.label: Storefronts
columns.definition: Yes if the product gives a creator a custom storefront or site that can take the place of building their own website (bio page, creator site, branded shop). Not a shop tab on someone else’s multi-seller marketplace.

columns.label: Marketplaces
columns.definition: Yes if a typical person can search and shop a catalog of offerings from many sellers, courses, books, digital goods, etc. Storefront software (Shopify, WooCommerce) is not a marketplace unless shoppers browse many sellers there.

scaleFacts: Network of ≈11M members; reviews cite 5M+ monthly visitors browsing the marketplace.
Catalog: photos, graphics, fonts, illustrations, icons, templates, themes, mockups, 3D models, and brushes.
Sellers upload digital files and licenses; buyers download immediately. Licensing: Personal, Commercial, Extended Commercial.
Buyer memberships (Growth–Studio) USD 19.95–99.95/month with curated monthly drops (up to ~USD 1000 value), 10–20% discounts, and monthly credits equal to plan price.

strengths.title: Large, targeted audience of design buyers
strengths.detail: Millions of buyers focused on creative content, sellers get instant access to a design-focused market.

strengths.title: Rich, professionally made asset catalog
strengths.detail: High-quality ready-to-use assets for small businesses and creators who need branding without a full-time designer.

strengths.title: Immediate digital delivery and licensing clarity
strengths.detail: Instant downloads with clear Personal / Commercial / Extended tiers for compliance.

strengths.title: Membership value for frequent buyers
strengths.detail: Monthly curated bundles, credits, and discounts can cut asset costs for heavy users.

weaknesses.title: Asset-centric, not community-centric
weaknesses.detail: Marketplace transactions first, limited native community vs creator-membership platforms.

weaknesses.title: Licensing complexity for novices
weaknesses.detail: Personal vs Commercial vs Extended can confuse buyers who don’t read terms carefully.

weaknesses.title: Competitive environment for sellers
weaknesses.detail: Large catalog means intense competition; sellers must optimize listings and marketing to stand out.

content:
Kahana is a library of curated hubs, Explore, Clubs, and optional Stripe. Creative Market is marketplace for design assets, fonts, templates, and creative digital goods. They overlap in places and diverge in others.

What each one is

Kahana is built around hubs people can open, Explore so strangers can find them, Aura as scarce daily recognition, and Clubs so discussion outlives a feed. Selling stays optional.

Creative Market is an online marketplace where creative professionals sell digital design assets, templates, graphics, fonts, photos, and more, to buyers around the world. Official site.

Why this comparison

This article puts Kahana and Creative Market side by side. It covers what each supports as a first-class product job, key features, and a few research notes so you have a clearer picture of what they are, how they compare, and what you can actually do on each one. It is not a teardown, and it is not a switch-tomorrow pitch.
contentAfter:
What you can do on each

On Kahana you can publish a hub, list it on Explore, discuss it in a Club, grant Aura, and turn on a Stripe paywall when you are ready to charge.

On Creative Market you can use Memberships and Marketplaces as first-class product jobs. The SKU is the product: a file, a theme, a craft listing, or a store you already operate.

Using Kahana with Creative Market

You can use both. Creative Market keeps doing what it already does well. Kahana is another place to package the work, get discovered, and grow an audience.

Keep Creative Market for SKUs you already sell well. Put the curated collection on Kahana: a public hub on Explore, Aura as signal, and Stripe when you want a second place people can find and pay.
